newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close mixed, unaffected by budget.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close mixed, unaffected by budget.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed mixed with a positive bias on Thursday in trendless trading that was unaffected by parliament's preliminary approval of the 1997 budget, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.38 percent, or 0.70 points, to 187.03 on turnover of 40 million shekels against 47 million on Thursday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.12 percent to 197.14.
"The market is very sleepy and activity is extremely low. Many Mishtanim shares were not traded and others moved sharply on thin volume," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblagon Securities.
"The (preliminary) approval of the budget is meaningless and the main question is what hidden promises were given to coalition members," Eidelheit said.

Parliament on Wednesday gave preliminary approval for the government's controversial 1997 budget. The 190.8 billion shekel budget, which cuts spending by 4.9 billion shekels, is being challenged by coalition members who say it hurts lower-income groups.

Gesher, a faction in the ruling Likud party led by Foreign Minister David Levy, dropped its opposition to the legislation in return for a letter from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu promising to consider changes in the budget before a final vote in parliament by year's end.
"Absolutely nothing is happening in the market and it is really dead. Everything is accidental and there is no clear trend," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
American Israeli Paper Mills Ltd rose 3.75 percent to 12,171. On Wednesday the company announced a cash dividend of $4.20 a share, reflecting capital gains due to a joint venture with Kimberly-Clark.

The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 133,653 on volume of 3.3 million shekels. Lehman Brothers cut its full-year earnings per share estimate for Teva but maintained its buy recommendation.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 28,181 on volume of 2.6 million shekels and Africa Israel Investments, which fell 1.0 percent to 411,080 on turnover of 1.6 million shekels.
